rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a Roberts opinion grounding the holding in Sosa’s “great caution,” Central Bank’s anti-implication principle, and Jesner/Nestlé separation-of-powers and foreign-relations concerns, with the TVPA as confirming context. One or more concurrences (especially Thomas or Gorsuch) may press an even narrower, more textual/jurisdictional view of § 1350, while Kagan is the most likely dissenter emphasizing aiding-and-abetting as an internationally recognized mode of liability.
